case.background: Liquid exits a small opening from a large maintained reservoir. The free surface and outlet are at the same pressure; free-surface speed, viscosity, and outlet losses are negligible. Determine how exit speed changes with liquid head and outlet area in this idealized rig.
initial_observations: The measured exit speed is stable while the selected head is maintained.

controls.description: Vertical liquid height above the outlet center.
controls.name: liquid_head_m

controls.description: Area of the small outlet opening.
controls.name: orifice_area_mm2

instruments.description: A large constant-head tank of incompressible, inviscid liquid with interchangeable small outlet plates and an optical exit-speed meter.
instruments.name: constant_head_efflux_tank

notes: This is a deterministic idealized benchmark world, not a literal replay of a historical data table.
A valid experiment changes only listed controls and consumes one episode attempt.
The ideal assumptions make the exit speed sqrt(2*g*head); outlet area changes volume flow, but not the reported speed.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'efflux_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_speed_m_per_s, head_exponent, area_exponent. Candidate law: v = reference_speed_m_per_s*(liquid_head_m/1 m)^head_exponent*(orifice_area_mm2/5 mm^2)^area_exponent

readouts.description: Mean liquid speed immediately outside the outlet.
readouts.name: exit_speed_m_per_s

case.title: Identify the liquid-head efflux relation
